When add() fails, the completion logs, hops to the MainActor and calls NotificationThresholdTracker.unmark. unmark removes the mark only if it still equals the failed threshold, so a higher mark set in the meantime is never undone. Tests use a fake center and never reach the real one. 3) Reversal: with the unmark call removed, failed_add_is_resent went RED again with the same line; with it restored, 13/13 passed. Mutation check: dropping the 'highestNotified[key] == threshold' guard makes unmark_keeps_higher_mark fail at NotificationThresholdTrackerTests.swift:92. 4) Retry cost: while authorization stays denied, every refresh tick with a window at or above its threshold makes one failed add() and writes one lifecycle error log line. That is about 1 per 300 s per affected window, with nothing shown to the user. 5) Also done: the DiskCacheTests rename is reverted (payload_age_uses_injected_clock), and the doc-comment example now reads 'Claude — 5h at 92%'. 6) This changes app behavior (a notification can be retried), so it needs a version bump, which auto-tag handles as a patch.
